title: Defensive tool-call schema + localized error-codes and compatibility shim
text:
Defensive tool-call schema + localized error-codes and compatibility shim

description:
Goal: define and implement a defensive JSON schema format and runtime validation + localized error-code surface for function/tool calling. This ticket covers: 1) a compact authoring format for call parameter schemas that is forward/backwards compatible with the legacy 'params' shape, 2) runtime coercion and graceful fallback rules (compatibility shim), 3) a machine- and user-friendly error envelope with stable error_code values and localized user messages, and 4) a migration plan and tests. Motivation: incidents where clients surface raw parser messages, ambiguous HTTP 400/422, and inconsistent error codes across SDKs cause poor UX and make alerts noisy. We want a predictable mapping from schema failure -> stable error_code -> suggested remediation that can be surfaced in Console, SDKs, and logs.

decision_summary:
We will introduce a thin compatibility shim: accept both legacy 'params' and new 'arguments' top-level keys, coercing types where safe (string->number if parseable, numeric string->number) and rejecting ambiguous cases. All validation errors will be normalized to the new "error-envelope v1" (fields: error_code, error_type, message, user_hint, data_path, locale_messages). Error codes will be short token strings (eg VALIDATION_MISSING_FIELD, VALIDATION_TYPE_MISMATCH, INTERNAL_RUNTIME_OVERLOAD) and are intended to be stable across minor runtime releases. Localized user-facing messages live in the Console/SDK layer and will be keyed by the error_code and locale. Security review required because schema input touches deserialization rules and type coercion.

schema_outline:
Authoring format (compact JSON) example:
{
  "name": "send_email",
  "arguments": {
    "recipient": {"type": "string", "format": "email", "required": true},
    "body": {"type": "string", "required": true},
    "priority": {"type": "integer", "enum": [1,2,3], "default": 2}
  },
  "compat": {"legacy_params_key": "params"}
}
Notes: - Minimal surface (type, required, enum, default, format) to keep runtime validation cheap. - Schema version is implicit in the runtime header; we will add explicit "schema_version" if/when we need breaking changes. - Arrays are supported with "items": {"type": "string"}

acceptance_criteria:
Runtime accepts both 'params' and 'arguments' top-level keys and applies coercion rules documented in the ticket.
Validation failures produce the error-envelope v1 JSON with stable 'error_code' and 'user_hint' fields.
Console and SDKs can map error_code -> localized message via a lookup table (proof: Console displays localized error for fr-FR and en-US).
Backcompat: existing clients that send numeric-as-string for integer fields are accepted if parseable; ambiguous coercions (eg '01' for octal intent) are rejected and produce VALIDATION_TYPE_MISMATCH.
Unit + integration tests covering 18 negative and 12 positive cases are added, CI enforces them, and a migration doc is published in Confluence.

implementation_notes:
Add a validation layer in the request ingress that runs before routing to the serving stack (low-latency code path). Keep validation synchronous and cheap: type checks, enum checks, required checks, simple format checks (email, uri).
Coercion rules: string->number if parseFloat(value).toString() === value or after trimming; boolean coercion only for exact strings 'true'|'false' (case-insensitive). Document that coercion is opportunistic and off by default for enterprise-locked contracts.
Error envelope v1 fields: error_code (stable token), error_type (validation|system|rate_limit|auth), message (short machine message), user_hint (one-line remediation), data_path (JSON path to offending field), locale_messages (list of locales available). The HTTP status mapping is part of the envelope: validation->422, auth->401, rate_limit->429, system->500.
Expose a concise error mapping file in repo: infra/error_codes/validation_codes.csv for cross-team visibility. SDKs will ship a mapping to zh-CN, fr-FR, es-ES for initial locales.
Add a lightweight compatibility shim that rewrites legacy 'params' -> 'arguments' using the declared compat. It must be idempotent and log a deprecation metric for telemetry.

testing_plan:
Unit tests for coercion rules (parseable numeric strings, boolean strings): run in test suites 'validation/unit'
Integration test: send legacy 'params' payloads and assert no regression; route through Canary cluster before global rollout
E2E: generate bad payloads from fuzz corpus and confirm stable error_codes are returned and do not leak stack traces
Localization test: mock SDK mapping for fr-FR and ensure Console shows translated 'user_hint' and message

comments:
2026-03-02 Maya Chen: Initial draft posted; flagged potential ambiguity around '0x' prefixed numeric strings. Decided to treat any non-decimal prefix as non-parseable.
2026-03-04 Pedro Alvarez (review): +1 on error envelope; request that we include a short code for telemetry (numeric metric id). Carlos to add mapping table.
2026-03-06 Design (Anika Patel): UX approves 'user_hint' field and suggests a second, shorter 'console_hint' for compact UI surfaces.
2026-03-08 Security (Liam O'Neil): Security review requested; raised deserialization concerns for date format parsing. Recommendation: avoid automatic date parsing; require explicit format and schema 'format': 'date' to accept. Marked as resolved.
2026-03-09 Carlos Rivera: Implemented runtime shim and added deprecation metric. PR 8312 opened for review. Added basic unit tests.

follow_up_tasks:
Ship SDK mapping for en-US, fr-FR, es-ES, zh-CN (PM/SDK owners) - PM to coordinate
Add schema_version field for v2 breaking changes proposal (spike ENG-141000)
Telemetry: add histogram for frequency of coercion events and top 10 offending fields to internal dashboard
Rolling upgrade plan: deploy to canary, monitor validation error rate and deprecation metric for 48 hours, then gradual rollout
